{"alternatives": [

    "service": "Azure Container Apps",
    "sku": "Consumption",
    "details": "Linux, Consumption plan, web API container with autoscaling to zero-ish overnight; ~2 vCPU/4 GiB average over business hours, minimal replicas at night. Also replaces the 3 AKS worker nodes (c2) since Container Apps manages the compute.",
    "rationale": "Container Apps removes the AKS cluster management fee and the always-on worker VMs, billing only for active vCPU-seconds, which suits a business-hours peak with quiet nights.",
    "tradeoffs": [
      "Less control over Kubernetes internals, node configuration and networking than AKS",
      "Cold-start latency when scaling from zero overnight unless minimum replicas are set to 1",
      "Migration effort if the workload relies on Kubernetes-specific resources or operators"
    ],
    "also_replaces": ["c2"]
  },
  {
    "component_id": "c1",
    "service": "Azure App Service",
    "sku": "P1v3",
    "details": "Linux, 2 instances scaled out during business hours and down to 1 at night, web API deployed as a container or code; 1 vCPU 4 GiB per instance.",
    "rationale": "App Service replaces the AKS cluster and its node VMs with a managed PaaS plan that is typically cheaper for a single stateless web API with predictable daily load.",
    "tradeoffs": [
      "Fewer scaling and networking options than Kubernetes; scale-out rules must be configured by hand",
      "Not suitable if the API needs multiple services or sidecars beyond what App Service supports",
      "Requires refactoring if the deployment is Kubernetes-manifest based"
    ],
    "also_replaces": ["c2"]
  },

    "component_id": "c3",
    "service": "SQL Database",
    "sku": "General Purpose serverless, 4 vCore max",
    "details": "General Purpose serverless tier, max 4 vCore with auto-pause disabled or a 1-hour delay, min vCore 0.5; assumes roughly 30 to 40 percent average utilization across the day.",
    "rationale": "Serverless bills per vCore-second actually used, so the quiet overnight hours and idle periods cost far less than a fixed 4 vCore provisioned instance.",
    "tradeoffs": [
      "Resume latency after auto-pause can affect the first request if auto-pause is enabled",
      "Cost can exceed provisioned pricing if the database runs near full capacity most of the day",
      "Compute scales within the configured min and max, so bursts above the max are throttled"
    ]

    "rationale": "If the application does not need Premium features such as VNet injection, persistence or clustering, the Standard tier at a similar memory size is substantially cheaper.",
    "tradeoffs": [
      "No VNet injection or private endpoints on Standard tier, so network isolation is weaker",
      "No data persistence or geo-replication, so a restart loses cached data",
      "Standard tier is not an SLA-backed replicated cache in the same way as Premium with replicas"
